title: What first round vote share will Iliana Iotova win in the 2026 Bulgarian Presidential election?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage vote share received by Iliana Iotova in the first round of the Bulgarian presidential election scheduled to be held on October 25, 2026, as declared by the [Bulgarian Central Election Commission](https://results.cik.bg/).
fine_print: If the election is postponed or cancelled such that no result is declared on or before December 31, 2026, this question will be **annulled**.

comments.author: tejvn
comments.text:
## Historical Context

Bulgaria held its first direct presidential election in 1992 following the dissolution of the Warsaw Pact. Since then, Bulgaria has held a presidential election every 5 years.

| Year | Round 1 Winner                   | Winner Vote Share | Round 1 Runner-Up               | Runner-Up Vote Share |
| ---- | -------------------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------- |
| 1992 | Zhelyu Zhelev (SDS, incumbent)   | 44.66%            | Velko Valkanov (ind./BSP)       | 30.44%               |
| 1996 | Petar Stoyanov (ODS)             | 44.07%            | Ivan Marazov (BSP)              | 27.01%               |
| 2001 | Georgi Parvanov (BSP)            | 36.39%            | Petar Stoyanov (ODS, incumbent) | 34.95%               |
| 2006 | Georgi Parvanov (BSP, incumbent) | 64.05%            | Volen Siderov (Ataka)           | 21.49%               |
| 2011 | Rosen Plevneliev (GERB)          | 40.11%            | Ivaylo Kalfin (BSP)             | 28.96%               |
| 2016 | Rumen Radev (ind./BSP)           | 25.44%            | Tsetska Tsacheva (GERB)         | 21.96%               |
| 2021 | Rumen Radev (ind., incumbent)    | 49.42%            | Anastas Gerdzhikov (GERB–SDS)   | 22.83%               |

It is very likely that Iliana Iotova will take the greatest vote share in the first round and Andrey Gyurov will win the 2nd greatest vote share (reasoning described in the Current Polls and Forecasts section).

The Winner Vote Share column has a mean: 43.45% and sample standard deviation: 11.88%.

With the outliers in 2006 and 2016 removed, the new column has mean: 42.93% and standard deviation: 4.93%.

### Outlier Analysis

#### [2006](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Bulgarian_presidential_election)

Parvanov won a 64.05% vote share in the first round because 1) He had incumbent advantage, 2) Three major parties (BSP, NDSV, and DPS: spanning left, centre and the ethnic-Turkish liberals) consolidated around him, and 3) the opposition vote was badly split: the mainstream right did unite behind a single candidate, Nedelcho Beronov, but he took only 9.75%, while Siderov's Ataka party took 21.49% from the nationalists. BSP, NDSV, and DPS had a combined vote share of (30.95+19.88+12.81) 63.64% in the most recent Parliamentary election at that time (2005). In contrast, in the [most recent election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Bulgarian_parliamentary_election) (April 2026), the Progressive Bulgaria party (which backs Iotova) won only 43.91% of the vote share.

#### [2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bulgarian_presidential_election)

Radev won only a 25.44% vote share in the first round because the field was unusually crowded, with 21 registered candidates, resulting in both major blocs leaking vote share heavily to other candidates: nationalist Krasimir Karakachanov (United Patriots) took 14.97% and populist businessman Veselin Mareshki 11.17%, while DPS backed its own independent, Plamen Oresharski, on 6.63%. In contrast, Progressive Bulgaria currently has a strong party and coalition and is unlikely to fragment in the following 7 weeks.

## Current Polls and Forecasts

[Politico](https://www.politico.eu/europe-poll-of-polls/bulgaria/) currently estimates a 46% vote share for Progressive Bulgaria based on an aggregation of polls. Other parties are below 16%.

[Global Metrics poll](https://www.novinite.bg/articles/288142/global-metriks-kandidat-za-prezident-na-progresivna-balgariya-bi-poluchil-nay-visoka-podkrepa): A nationally representative poll (n\=1503) conducted June-July 2026 lists support for Iotova at 50%, Gyurov at 23%, and Valchev at 18%. The same poll lists support for Progressive Bulgaria at 39.7%, PP–DB at 13.3%, and GERB–SDS at 11.5%. This poll was conducted before Iotova announced her run for election on July 24. The question referred to above asks whether respondents would "rather or certainly" support the candidate. The same study reported support for Iotova ranging between 38% and 50% depending on the scenario tested.

As mentioned above, in the [April 2026 parliamentary election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Bulgarian_parliamentary_election), the PB Party (which backs Iotova) won 43.91% of the vote share.

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/Screenshot_2026-09-04_at_7.49.42PM.png "Polling and Election Data")

#### [](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Bulgarian_presidential_election)

Based on these polls and [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/bulgaria-presidential-election) data, it is very likely that Iliana Iotova will win the greatest vote share in the first round and Andrey Gyurov will win the 2nd greatest vote share. Iotova has a 71% implied probability of winning the election (the runoff, not the 1st round) while Gyurov has a 25% implied probability.

The Global Metrics poll is the most recent high-sample size poll conducted and is 2 months out of date (it was also conducted before Iotova announced her run for election). Additionally, in general, polls are notorious for carrying heavy systematic biases; the polls leading up to the parliamentary elections in April 2026 underestimated PB vote share by over 10pp.

## Forecast

My forecast has a median of 44.3% with a 50% CI of \[39.7%, 48.3%] and an 80% CI of \[35.0%, 51.8%].

**Median (44.3%):** Four independent anchors cluster tightly: the outlier-adjusted historical mean for first-round winners (42.93%), PB's April 2026 parliamentary result (43.91%), Politico's poll-of-polls estimate (46%), and the midpoint of Global Metrics' 38–50% range (44%).

**Why my credence intervals are wide:**

1. The most relevant published survey (Global Metrics) asks whether respondents would "rather or certainly" support each candidate (favorability, not vote choice) and itself reports Iotova ranging 38–50%. Fieldwork for the survey closed 11 July, before Iotova declared on 24 July and before the PB, BSP–OL, and Stand Up Bulgaria endorsements.
2. The deadline to run for election is September 22. GERB has no candidate and Kostadinov's bid is unconfirmed. Ticket count is the single largest determinant of a first-round share, and late entrants can easily reshape the race.

I expect my credence intervals to shrink considerably after September 22 when the field is finalized and as more up-to-date polling data is published.
